mechanism_narrative: Grocery-pharmacy mobility has risen from -0.3% to +2.1% week-on-week, signaling resumed essential shopping trips. This normalization of essential mobility reduces fear-driven avoidance and unlocks discretionary retail-recreation visits within the same weekly cycle, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean, or GROCERY_PHARM reverts to negative territory within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Parks mobility has improved from -28.7% (t-2w) to -6.0% (t-0w), indicating outdoor activity substitution is weakening. As outdoor recreation becomes less attractive or accessible, consumers redirect discretionary time and spending to indoor retail-recreation venues, producing net positive RETAIL_REC momentum over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 22.7 percentage points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or remains flat over the next 28 days despite PARKS remaining above -10%, or PARKS reverses below -15%.

mechanism_narrative: Transit-station mobility remains severely depressed at -31.7%, constraining commuter access to retail clusters. If transit does not recover above -25% within two weeks, retail-recreation mobility will remain suppressed due to reduced foot traffic from commuters. Conversely, any transit recovery above -25% will unlock retail gains.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -25% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -31.7% (t-0w), no recovery trend visible
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises above -20% within two weeks and RETAIL_REC simultaneously increases, contradicting the suppression mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility has declined from +6.1% (t-2w) to +4.4% (t-0w), indicating residents are spending less time at home and more time outside. This outbound mobility shift, combined with rising GROCERY_PHARM (+2.1%), signals a broader reopening of public activity. The interaction of reduced home-time and normalized essential shopping drives retail-recreation recovery over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines below +5% AND GROCERY_PHARM rises above 0%

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean, or RESIDENTIAL rebounds above +6% while GROCERY_PHARM reverts negative.

mechanism_narrative: Workplace mobility has stabilized at -8.3% (t-1w and t-0w) after declining from -9.3%, suggesting partial return-to-office policies are taking hold. Stable workplace presence enables weekday retail-recreation visits by commuters and office workers, producing sustained RETAIL_REC gains over the next four weeks if workplace stability persists.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES stabilizes within ±1 percentage point for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -8.3% for both t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES declines below -10% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days remains below the prior 28-day mean despite workplace stability.

mechanism_narrative: The four-week trend shows RETAIL_REC improving from -12.7% to -9.7%, a consistent +3 percentage-point recovery. If this linear trend continues, RETAIL_REC will reach approximately -6.7% by week t+4w. This seasonal or cyclical recovery pattern, independent of external shocks, will drive RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 3.0 percentage points over four weeks (t-3w to t-0w)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean, or the week-on-week improvement rate reverses to negative for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Transit mobility at -31.7% and workplace mobility at -8.3% show a large gap, indicating workers are not commuting via public transit. If transit recovers faster than workplace mobility over the next two weeks (closing the gap by >5 points), it signals policy-driven transit reopening that will unlock retail-recreation access, driving RETAIL_REC gains. Failure to close this gap maintains retail suppression.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by >5 percentage points while WORKPLACES remains stable
failure_condition: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES gap does not narrow by >5 points within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean.
